subject.title: fix(update): dev channel update builds from an unverified checkout at the git install path

question: Should package-to-dev conversion permanently reject every existing path, including empty directories and user-maintained canonical OpenClaw checkouts?
rationale: Remote inspection cannot prove a checkout safe, but categorical refusal changes a documented setup workflow and requires operator action for existing users; automation should not choose that security-versus-compatibility contract.

options.title: Require fresh paths
options.body: Keep the fail-closed fresh-clone rule, move retry ownership to SQLite, and explicitly document the one-time operator action.

options.title: Design explicit migration
options.body: Add a separately approved flow that preserves an existing directory only by cloning verified source elsewhere and atomically replacing it without executing the old checkout.

recommendation.title: Require fresh paths
recommendation.body: Keep the fail-closed fresh-clone rule, move retry ownership to SQLite, and explicitly document the one-time operator action.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent history spans both updater verification and security workflow behavior, which matches this security and compatibility decision.
